text: . A small unblinded study1 involving 7 patients has suggested that flunarizine is more effective than pla- cebo in the treatment of Tourette’s syndrome (see Tics, p.954). 1. Micheli F, et al. Treatment of Tourette’s syndrome with calcium antagonists. Clin Neuropharmacol 1990; 13: 77–83. Vertigo. Antihistamines are the mainstay of the treatment of vertigo (p.565). However, their antimuscarinic adverse effects may prove troublesome, particularly in the elderly, and they pro- duce central sedation. Flunarizine is devoid of antimuscarinic properties, although it may produce central sedation.
